description: We're a team of software engineers and 1st-place winners of SENTEC The Engineer's Code 2026. We're building a web app that harmonizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS hotspot records into one consistent time series and shows it as an interactive burning activity calendar, with historical comparisons and anomaly detection for any selected area. We bring strong full-stack web and data dashboard skills.
summary:
Five NASA satellites watch Pakistan for fires, but MODIS and VIIRS see so differently that their raw counts cannot be compared: the yearly count jumped six times in 2012 only because a sharper satellite started counting. BlindSpot fuses 5.6 million MODIS and VIIRS detections (2000 to 2026) into one harmonized fire record for every one of Pakistan's 126 districts, on a single scale learned from the years when all five satellites flew together. Leave-one-year-out tests show the monthly error falls from 55% to 7.5% once VIIRS is in the sky.
The timing makes it urgent. On 2 November 2026 NASA stopped Suomi NPP fire data. BlindSpot measured that 23.3% of Pakistan's fire events (67,288 fires) were seen by Suomi NPP and no other satellite, up to 28% in Faisalabad and Toba Tek Singh, and shows exactly where and when those fires now go unrecorded. It is a free website anyone can use: a daily burning calendar, a failure simulator, a Blind Clock of unwatched hours with the best hours for field checks, a map of year-round industrial heat, shareable district scorecards, live alerts, CSV export and an AI assistant that answers in plain language. Crop burning is a major source of Punjab's smog, so a fair, honest fire record matters for health and for policy.
details:
What it does. BlindSpot is a free website that turns every NASA FIRMS fire detection over Pakistan since November 2000 into one consistent burning record per district, and measures what that record loses when a satellite stops. Pick any of 126 districts or type any town; every view follows that place.

  • Burning calendar: 27 years, one square per day, harmonized fire events, with unusual days outlined (more fires than that time of year normally has). Click a day to see its fires on a map and which satellites saw each one.
  • Fire history and outlook: month-by-year heatmap, this month against the historical median, a season race (is this rice or wheat season burning faster than the last five?) and a 14-day climatology outlook.
  • Lost Eyes: the fires only one satellite saw, by month, by fire size and by district, with a blind-spot map coloured by the share each district loses without Suomi NPP.
  • Failure simulator: switch any of the five satellites off and every fire event from the three years when all five flew is recounted in the browser.
  • Blind Clock: satellite overpass times learned from the detections themselves (with the drifting Terra and Aqua at this year's times), showing the hours no fire satellite watches Pakistan (about 4 PM to 8:30 PM local time) and a countdown to the next pass. Its Burn Window Advisor says whether a district is watched right now and gives the best hours for field checks.
  • Live now: today's NASA FIRMS fires, fused the same way and compared with each district's own history to raise alerts.
  • Industrial heat: 186 year-round hot spots (the same 1 km spot hot on 60+ days across 8+ months), likely brick kilns, gas flares and factories. They are kept out of the crop-fire record and mapped on their own, with a filter for those still hot in the smog season and a satellite view of each spot.
  • District scorecards: a shareable page with its own preview image for every district and province: fire rank, this season against the usual for the same dates, the share of fires only Suomi NPP saw, and the Trust Score.
  • Area and export: any circle on the map analysed on the fly and downloadable as CSV (every fire event, a daily calendar or a monthly summary), plus a printable district report.
  • Ask BlindSpot AI: questions in plain language, answered by calling tools over the site's own data; a server check compares every number in the answer against the data before it is shown.
  • Made for first-time visitors: a short welcome guide, an "in plain words" line on every tab, and tap-to-explain for terms like harmonized and FRP.

How it works.

  1. Download all MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) detections for Pakistan plus a 15 km buffer: 5.6 million detections.
  2. Remove swath duplicates and fuse detections of the same fire on the same local day (750 m clustering) into 3.5 million fire events, keeping which satellites saw each one.
  3. Remove 1.4 million persistent heat sources (brick kilns, gas flares, industry) found by repeat detection in the same grid cell.
  4. Harmonize: for each satellite era, learn per province and calendar month how many events today's five-satellite constellation records for each event that era's satellites recorded, using the overlap years. Every day is rescaled to the full-constellation view, so a rise means more fire, not more satellites. FRP from MODIS is calibrated to the VIIRS scale with matched pairs, per MODIS pixel size; the How it works page shows the matched pairs before and after calibration.
  5. Validate by leaving each fire-year out and predicting it: monthly count error drops from 97% to 55% (Terra only), 91% to 29% (Terra and Aqua), 55% to 7.5% (with Suomi NPP) and 21% to 3.1% (today's constellation). Each district also gets a Trust Score from agreement, coverage, stability and sample size.
  6. Publish static JSON and run everything in the browser; the site is Next.js on Vercel, with no database.

Why it matters. Stubble burning in Punjab feeds the smog that closes schools in Lahore every winter. Agencies, researchers and journalists need a fire record that is comparable across years, and need to know what the satellite record no longer sees after Suomi NPP. BlindSpot answers both, at district level, for free. The pipeline takes any bounding box, so the same method works for any country.

Tools. Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, GeoPandas), TypeScript, Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL, Vercel.

Source code. https://github.com/huzaifashahid9/BlindSpot (public repo with the full data pipeline and the web app).
